why: The doc sentence is verbatim (setup.md:227, whole line read; the following bullets confirm latest=default / stable, and nothing later in the section reverses it), and the cited line is real (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts:127 is exactly `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true`). The finding still fails on all three of the remaining checks. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM / deliberate product difference. `autoUpdatesChannel` governs the Claude Code CLI's own self-updater: the native installer's `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` tree, `claude update`, npm-global installs, Homebrew cask names (`claude-code` vs `claude-code@latest`), `minimumVersion`, `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` -- the whole surrounding section of setup.md is about that mechanism. Nessy Desktop has no such updater and no `nessy update` command (apps/cli/src has no self-update path at all); it is an Electron app updated by electron-updater from an internal T-Bank S3 feed of dmg/nsis/AppImage artifacts. `setup.md` is already row 152 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md with the recorded verdict `vne produkta` (out of product), alongside `platforms`, `quickstart`, `troubleshoot-install`, `vs-code`. (2) THE CLAIMED ABSENCE EVIDENCE IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. `grep -rain autoUpdatesChannel packages/ apps/ scripts/` does NOT return 0 hits -- it hits 5 files: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js, apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js and their apps/electron/dist/ copies. The vendored agent-SDK bundle carries the key as `autoUpdatesChannel: z.enum(["latest","stable","rc"]).optional()` -- three values, not the two the finding asserts -- next to `minimumVersion`/`requiredMinimumVersion`. So the finding both mis-states its own grep and mis-states the shipped enum. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE: a release channel DOES reach the updater. apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80 sets `channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"` in the `publish:` block; electron-builder bakes it into `app-update.yml` and electron-updater uses it to select the `dev-mac.yml` / `dev-arm64-mac.yml` / `dev-win.yml` metadata the feed publishes (the same names scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs:34-94 builds from its `--channel`). .gitlab-ci.yml:234-235 sets it (`NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL=dev`) and :368,:389 verify the feed against `${NESSY_DESKTOP_DEV_UPDATE_CHANNEL:-dev}`. The channel is therefore wired end to end -- it is build/ops-owned rather than user-selectable, which is not what the finding claims. There is also only ONE published train (`dev`), so a runtime latest-vs-stable selector would have nothing to choose between. Minor extra overstatement: `autoDownload` is not unconditional in effect -- checkForUpdates() overrides it per call at auto-update.ts:333-334 and restores at :369, so the manual Settings 'Check for updates' path can check without downloading.
correctedState: Not a divergence. `autoUpdatesChannel` is a Claude Code CLI self-updater setting (native-installer versions tree, `claude update`, npm/Homebrew trains) and setup.md is already scored out-of-product as row 152 of the coverage map. Nessy Desktop is an Electron app on electron-updater against an internal S3 feed and ships no CLI self-updater. It does have a release channel wired to the updater -- apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80 `channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"`, baked into app-update.yml, set to `dev` by .gitlab-ci.yml:235 and verified by scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs -- it is build/ops-owned, not a user setting, and only one train (`dev`) is published, so there is no second channel to select. The finding's grep evidence is also wrong: `autoUpdatesChannel` appears in 5 bundled files (pi-agent-server and session-mcp-server dists) as a three-value enum `["latest","stable","rc"]`, not 0 hits and not two values.
